settings.aboutTitle: Twelve years of helping students rise
settings.aboutText: Smartup began in 2014 with 63 students in one centre in Kochi. Today more than 30,000 students have learned with us, online and at 9 centres across Kochi.

vision.title: Shaping the future of learning
text: Smartup believes every child has a brighter future within them. With the right guidance, encouragement and learning support, that potential can become exceptional.

We do more than impart knowledge: we discover each student’s strengths, nurture their capabilities and help them grow with confidence. Our goal is to become a trusted, globally recognised K–12 education brand, connecting students across India and the GCC with accessible, high-quality learning, personalised guidance and technology that supports every learner.

priorities.title: A global education network
priorities.text: Expand across the GCC while strengthening our presence in Kerala, as a trusted brand for students and families.

priorities.title: Personalised, technology-enabled learning
priorities.text: Digital tools and AI that tailor lessons to each student, find knowledge gaps and show clear progress.

priorities.title: Academic excellence
priorities.text: High-quality Kerala State and CBSE learning through excellent teachers, structured systems and consistent support.

priorities.title: Online and offline, at scale
priorities.text: Online learning connected to a growing network of centres, serving more students without losing quality.

priorities.title: Accessible education for every student
priorities.text: Quality learning for students from every background, so each learner can build confidence and reach their potential.

vision.vision2030: Vision 2030: keep mentoring students beyond Class 12, through higher education and into careers — and bring 500+ professionals mentored by Smartup together on one stage in 2030.

settings.companyVision: To be established as the most trusted academic partner for students by setting a benchmark of excellence in education.

leaders.name: Mohamed Rayees
leaders.photoAlt: Mohamed Rayees speaking at Talent Eve
leaders.summary: Leads Smartup's mentoring initiatives, including Coffee With Chairman, Talent Eve and Shoot the Drugs.
leaders.bio: Mohamed Rayees is the Chairman and CEO of Smartup, with over a decade of experience in education and student development. He leads initiatives that combine quality education, meaningful mentorship and opportunities for students to build confidence, discipline and life skills — including Coffee With Chairman (CWC), Talent Eve and Shoot the Drugs. His Vision 2030 commits Smartup to mentoring students beyond Class 12, through higher education and into careers.

posts.title: A 90-day plan for the SSLC and CBSE Class 10 board exams
posts.excerpt: Three months is enough time to revise every chapter twice — if you plan it. Here is the plan our teachers share with every Class 10 batch.
posts.body:
## Days 1–30: finish the first round

List every chapter in every subject and give each one a date. Aim to finish one full round of revision in the first month, even if some chapters feel rushed. Mark each chapter green, yellow or red as you go.

## Days 31–60: practise with past papers

Spend this month on previous years' questions. Solve one paper a week under exam conditions and correct it the same day. Every mistake goes into a single notebook, sorted by chapter.

- Start with your red chapters
- Time yourself on every paper
- Read the marking scheme, not just the answer

## Days 61–90: second round and rest

Revise from your mistakes notebook, not from the textbook. Keep two days a week lighter, and sleep at the same time every night. The last week is for short revision only.

**Need help building your plan?** Our teachers do this with every batch. [Book a free demo class](https://smartupedu.in/demo) or call +91 88919 10919.

posts.title: Five ways parents can help during board exam season
posts.excerpt: Your child does the studying, but home sets the pace. Small, steady habits from parents make a real difference before board exams.
posts.body:
## 1. Keep a steady routine

Regular meals, sleep and study hours matter more than long nights. A predictable day lowers stress for everyone.

## 2. Ask about plans, not marks

Instead of asking for scores, ask what your child will revise today. It keeps the focus on effort they control.

## 3. Make space to study

A quiet corner, good light and a phone parked in another room help more than any new book.

## 4. Stay in touch with teachers

Read the weekly and monthly updates, and come to parent meetings. Teachers can tell you exactly which chapters need attention.

## 5. Celebrate small wins

A finished chapter or a better test score deserves notice. Confidence grows from many small successes.

At Smartup, parents receive regular progress updates and meet teachers through the year. [Talk to our team](https://smartupedu.in/contact) to learn how it works.

posts.title: Why ten minutes of daily practice beats a night of cramming
posts.excerpt: Short daily quizzes build memory that lasts until the exam. Here is why, and how to make it a habit.
posts.body:
## Memory needs repetition

When you recall something a day after learning it, your brain strengthens the path to that memory. Cramming skips those repeats, so most of it fades within days.

## How we use it in class

Every Smartup class ends with a short daily quiz on the previous topic. It takes about ten minutes, and it shows students and teachers exactly what needs another look.

## Build the habit at home

- Pick one subject each evening
- Write five quick questions from today's class
- Answer them tomorrow before you open the book
- Mark anything you missed and try it again on Sunday

Ten focused minutes a day add up to more than a whole night before the exam — and they leave you rested on exam day.

faqs.question: Which classes and boards do you teach?
faqs.answer: Smartup teaches classes 8 to 12 (Plus One and Plus Two) for CBSE and Kerala State Board students, at 9 centres in Kochi and online.

faqs.question: How do I book a free demo class?
faqs.answer: Call +91 88919 10919 or visit your nearest centre between 5 and 9 pm. Our team will arrange a free demo class for your child.

faqs.question: How can I find out about fees and admissions?
faqs.answer: Call +91 88919 10919 or contact your nearest centre. The team will explain the relevant programme, fees, payment options and current batch availability.

faqs.question: What is the difference between Smartup Pro, Trio and Power?
faqs.answer: Smartup Pro is one-to-one, with a student diagnosis, a personalised learning plan, mentorship and monthly parent meetings. Smartup Trio teaches three students together, with mentorship, regular evaluations and parent meetings every two months. Smartup Power is a micro batch with competency-based learning, daily, weekly and monthly evaluations, and quarterly parent meetings.

faqs.question: How long is each class?
faqs.answer: In our CBSE programmes, Class 8 sessions run 1 hour 30 minutes, Classes 9 and 10 run 1 hour 45 minutes, and Plus One and Plus Two run 2 hours. State Board sessions run about 2 hours. Each session includes teaching, a short daily quiz, corrections and time for doubts.

faqs.question: Do you follow my school's syllabus?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our CBSE programmes strictly follow each student's school syllabus, and State Board classes are built around SCERT texts and board-style questions.

faqs.question: Can I join a State Board batch?
faqs.answer: Yes. Contact your nearest centre for the subjects, timings and formats available for your class.

faqs.question: How will I know how my child is doing?
faqs.answer: Parents in Smartup Pro and Trio receive a weekly update on attendance, topics completed, homework and test performance. Every programme sends a monthly report with marks, improvement, strengths, weak areas, teacher remarks and next month's target.

faqs.question: Will my child have a mentor?
faqs.answer: Yes. Mentors follow up on attendance, homework and motivation, and keep parents informed. In Smartup Pro each mentor looks after up to 10 students; in Smartup Trio, up to 20.

faqs.question: Where are your centres and when are they open?
faqs.answer: Chullickal, Kadavanthra, Eraveli, Thoppumpady, Palluruthy, Moolamkuzhi, Fort Kochi, Vennala and Edappally. All centres are open from 5 to 9 pm.

faqs.question: Can my child study online?
faqs.answer: Yes. Our CBSE and State Board programmes run online, with an AI-integrated learning app and LMS, WhatsApp learning groups and live exam-preparation sessions on YouTube.

faqs.question: Is there a Smartup app?
faqs.answer: Yes. The Smartup Learning app is on the App Store and Google Play. Students use it for class notes, recorded classes and revision sessions.

faqs.question: What are Coffee With Chairman, Talent Eve and Shoot the Drugs?
faqs.answer: Coffee With Chairman (CWC) is a mentoring programme led by our Chairman, Mohamed Rayees. Talent Eve is our award ceremony and arts festival. Shoot the Drugs is a sports tournament that spreads awareness against drug abuse.
